During the hearing on 6.9.2023, the learned counsel for Respondent TANGEDCO opposed the IA and submitted that in view of changes in the pleadings and tariff filing forms, the Petitioner should be directed to withdraw the present Petition and file a fresh tariff Petition. In response, the learned counsel for the Petitioner clarified that the IA had been filed to place on record the actual data for the year 2021–22, which was earlier claimed on a projection basis, along with an additional prayer seeking relaxation of ATQ due to COVID, and that the tariff filing forms had been substituted with revised calculations. Considering the parties' submissions and noting that the IA formed part of and was in continuation of the original Petition, the Commission admitted the IA and issued notice to the Respondents. The Petitioner was also directed to file additional information, which was submitted vide an affidavit dated 3.11.2023, and the Respondents, TANGEDCO and BSPHCL, filed their replies vide separate affidavits dated 2.12.2023 and 4.12.2023, respectively. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner sought permission to file an additional affidavit revising the forms/documents pertaining to the year 2023-24 and to place the same on record. The learned counsels for the Respondents TANGEDCO and MSEDCL sought time to file their replies to the additional affidavit to be submitted by the Petitioner. 32. In compliance with the said direction, the Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 1.10.2024, has filed additional submissions after serving a copy on the Respondents. Replies have been filed by the Respondents MSEDCL and BSPHCL vide affidavits dated 16.10.2024 and 17.10.2024, respectively. Rejoinders to these replies have been filed by the Petitioner vide affidavits dated 22.10.2024. 36. After hearing the learned counsels for both the Petitioner and the Respondents at length, and carefully considering their respective submissions, written pleadings and relevant material on record, the issues have been examined, and the same are dealt with in succeeding paragraphs. 43. It is noticed that the Petitioner has provided a detailed chronology explaining the sequence of events that led to the delay in land acquisition. The material on record indicates that the delay was not due to any inaction or negligence on the part of the Petitioner, but was largely attributable to external factors such as changes in the State R&R policy, delay in approval of the R&R plan by the State Government, resistance from villagers, law and order problems and encroachments on land. Perusal of the records further reveals that the Petitioner consistently engaged with the District Administration and other government authorities and undertook persistent efforts to resolve the issues affecting land acquisition. These actions demonstrate that the Petitioner exercised due diligence in pursuing the matter with the concerned authorities. 44. In view of the detailed justification and supporting documents furnished by the Petitioner, including communications with government authorities and evidence relating to law and order disturbances, we are satisfied that the delay in land acquisition and consequent delay in commencement of production occurred due to circumstances beyond the control of the Petitioner. Accordingly, we are of the view that the delay in the commencement of production on account of land acquisition issues constitutes an uncontrollable factor. Considering the documentary evidence and the circumstances of the case, the delay in executing the project and commencing production is therefore condoned. 81.
